episodes.190848: A cold front tracking eastward across Montana generated a line of severe thunderstorms   across the eastern half of the state, from late afternoon through the early nighttime hours.  This line eventually moved east into North Dakota.
episodes.190866: Deep atmospheric mixing within vicinity of a surface dryline near the Texas/New Mexico state line allowed a cumulus field to develop. Strong southeasterly low level flow brought ample moisture into the region providing sufficient instability for severe thunderstorms. Moderate deep layer shear allowed isolated thunderstorms to become organized and severe, producing severe wind gusts and large hail over the southwestern South Plains. Additional thunderstorms developed late on the 15th in eastern New Mexico and drifted into the South Plains in the early morning hours of the 16th. This activity dissipated into light rain showers as it moved into the central South Plains. However, the sub-cloud layer was extremely dry which led to the rain evaporating before reaching the ground and causing a widespread heat burst from Hockley County into Lubbock and Lynn Counties. Temperatures increased as much as 24 degrees in 20 minutes as well as bringing severe wind gusts.||High wind gusts from the heat burst measured by the Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet are listed below:||75 mph at Wolfforth (Lubbock County),|66 mph at Levelland (Hockley County), and|59 mph at Tahoka (Lynn County).
episodes.190946: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across mainly the southern and western portions of Central Alabama during the afternoon of June 16 associated with southeasterly flow around the southwestern periphery of an upper-level ridge. Low-level moisture advancing northward into western Alabama contributed to thunderstorm activity, with one downburst producing minor damage in Tuscaloosa.
episodes.190961: A traditional summertime pattern set up over Middle Tennessee on June 16, 2024. While these pop-up thunderstorms were generally non-severe, a couple of them briefly became strong, downing trees, tree limbs, and power lines around the Nashville metro area.
episodes.191022: A severe thunderstorms produced strong winds, up to 74 mph, as it cross Washington County during the evening of June 15th.
episodes.191212: A waterspout was spotted offshore of Panama City Beach. In addition, strong storms moving northwestward through Apalachee Bay produced strong wind gusts in excess of 34 knots along the coast as they moved inland.
episodes.192025: Scattered thunderstorms were common across the Billings Forecast Area. Warm temperatures aloft, combined with dry lower levels, resulted in a few of these thunderstorms producing severe wind gusts.
episodes.192028: Scattered thunderstorms were common across the Billings Forecast Area. Warm temperatures aloft, combined with dry lower levels, resulted in a few of these thunderstorms producing severe wind gusts.
episodes.192300: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms developed along an advancing warm front during the morning of June 16th.  The storms remained well north of the I-74 corridor northward to I-80.  Some of the storms skirted across Stark County, resulting in minor wind damage and hail as large as quarters.
episodes.192420: A pair of nearly stationary storms developed in Southwest Nebraska during the late afternoon into the early evening and produced hail stones up to 4 inches in diameter.
episodes.192511: A mesoscale convective vortex produced windy thunderstorms as it moved across northern Illinois during the afternoon of the 16th. These storms developed a gust front which managed to kick up dust and significantly reduce visibilities across parts of Kane County.
episodes.192520: The combined OK/TX Panhandles were hit with a gusty line of storms both on the 13th and 14th of June. Severe winds were the main story with these storms. Ground stations measured wind gusts as high as 80 mph with the storms on the 13th. Then on the 14th, multiple reports of wind damage were made with estimated winds as high as 85 mph, as multiple train cars were knocked over in Cimarron County in OK along with a gain silo damaged in Dallam County in TX.  Then on the 15th Beaver County did see a discrete storm produce some large hail.
episodes.192570: A mesoscale convective vortex produced windy thunderstorms as it moved across northern Illinois and out over Lake Michigan on the 16th.
episodes.192726: Scattered convection developed during the afternoon hours in the Quad State, with storms tracking northeastward. Thunderstorm winds blew down multiple trees in Southwestern Illinois. MLCAPE was 2000-3000 J/kg while effective bulk shear was 25-30 kts.
episodes.192727: Scattered convection developed during the afternoon hours in the Quad State, with storms tracking northeastward. Damage occurred to a barn and some trees in Scott County, Missouri. MLCAPE was around 3000 J/kg while effective bulk shear was 25-30 kts.
episodes.192747: A Mesoscale Convective Vortex (MCV) moved through the region on the morning of June 16. This quick moving system produced widespread winds between 60 to 70 mph through it's path, especially for areas along and east of the Mississippi River. Isolated reports of hail were noted, with the largest being golf ball sized.
episodes.192748: A Mesoscale Convective Vortex (MCV) moved through the region on the morning of June 16. This quick moving system produced widespread winds between 60 to 70 mph through it's path, especially for areas along and east of the Mississippi River. Isolated reports of hail were noted, with the largest being golf ball sized.
episodes.192821: A wet period allowed for flooding to return to portions of the Little Sioux River. This was capped by a multi-day significant heavy rainfall event between June 20th through June 22nd which brought widespread rain totals between 5 and 10 inches with pockets in excess of 15 inches. As rainfall reached area streams and rivers, major to record flooding was observed, devastating several towns and communities. All river crest information is preliminary until made official by the gauge owner.
episodes.192832: A shortwave moving into the region resulted in showers and thunderstorms into the previous evening and continuing into the early morning hours on June 16th over the western half of Iowa. MLCAPE values around 1000-2000 J/kg and 20-30 knots of bulk shear allowed for a favorable environment to produce a few storms that become severe, with thunderstorm wind damage reported in Sac and Webster counties.
episodes.192877: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over eastern portions of Pennington County, producing wind gusts to around 60 mph from Wasta to near Wall.
episodes.192878: A severe thunderstorm developed over the Buffalo area in Harding County and tracked eastward across far northern Perkins County. The storm produced hail to over quarter size and gusty winds.
episodes.192879: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over central Fall River County, producing wind gusts to over 65 mph near Angostura Reservoir.
episodes.192880: A line of severe storms developed across western Jackson County and tracked east-northeast into central South Dakota. The storms produced hail to golf ball size and wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph.
episodes.192881: A thunderstorm produced wind gusts to near 65 mph across portions of southeast Oglala Lakota County.
episodes.192935: In the wake of a morning mesoscale convective system (MCS) across Nebraska, storms refired during the evening hours across northwest Iowa within fairly weak deep-layer shear and up to 2000 J/kg MUCAPE. Storms produced locally damaging wind as cores collapsed, and training of storms resulted in locally heavy rainfall of 2 to 3 inches around the Iowa Great Lakes in the matter of an hour or two.
episodes.192978: Slow moving thunderstorms in the Panama City Beach area produced flash flooding.
episodes.192983: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon, typical of summertime. The strongest storm produced isolated impacts.
episodes.193284: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours as a surface trough and upper level short wave trough moved through the area. Some of the storms became severe with the initial threat being large hail, with the largest hail the size of tennis balls in Hettinger County to the west of Lake Tschida. Later in the event, damaging wind gusts became the main concern. The greatest reported damage was in the Turtle Mountains region of north central North Dakota, where a movie drive in restaurant was severely damaged near Lake Metigoshie, and near Belcourt where a home, playground equipment, and trees were damaged.
episodes.193301: Isolated strong thunderstorms moved across southeast WI. One storm became severe producing tree damage.
episodes.193351: Clusters of severe storms moved northeast through the area, producing several areas of wind damage.
episodes.193595: Series of troughs enhanced afternoon convection during the week. Flooding, thunderstorm wind and hail reports were received at some point during the week. Activity caused a landslide in Bayamon. Lightning even struck the roof of a residence, causing injuries and damaged appliances, furniture, and the roof of the house.
episodes.193640: A late evening supercell thunderstorm moved through portions of west Texas and produced a few instances of large hail.
episodes.193700: An upper low moved into the region during the middle of June. An isolated severe storm occurred as a result.
episodes.193919: On the morning of the 15th, upper air analysis showed a shortwave trough centered over the High Plains. At the surface, a warm front draped across the Plains slowly lifted north throughout the day, eventually stalling out across eastern Nebraska and down into northwestern Missouri. That afternoon, two areas of thunderstorm development was noted, one in northeast Kansas and another in northeast Nebraska. The thunderstorms in northeast Kansas quickly grew upscale into an MCS bringing strong winds and a brief spin-up tornado to southeast Nebraska and southwest Iowa. The thunderstorms in northeast Nebraska were tied to a lingering MCV, with the storm mode initially remaining as clustered supercells. This brought large hail and several tornadoes across northeast Nebraska before finally growing upscale into a second MCS and tracking east into west-central Iowa.
episodes.193920: On the morning of the 15th, upper air analysis showed a shortwave trough centered over the High Plains. This brought large hail and several tornadoes across northeast Nebraska before finally growing upscale into a second MCS and tracking east into west-central Iowa.
episodes.193940: Developing sea breeze convection along the sea breeze produced a waterspout in Kings Bay that ultimately moved ashore near Crystal River in Citrus County.
episodes.193941: Developing sea breeze convection along the sea breeze produced a waterspout in Kings Bay that ultimately moved ashore near Crystal River in Citrus County, becoming a tornado and damaging two homes.
episodes.194134: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms moved across southeast WI and over the nearshore and opens waters of Lake Michigan.
episodes.194308: A complex of thunderstorms moved across the region on Sunday, June 16. Later that evening and overnight another complex of thunderstorms developed over south central Minnesota.

Based on chaser video as well as drone footage, this tornado developed 5.5 miles north of Clarkson, NE and moved east northeast. The tornado then produced EF-1 damage to a machine shed on a farmstead. The narrow tornado continued northeast another mile before lifting. Peak estimated winds in this tornado were at 101 miles per hour. The maximum width and average width of this tornado were both estimated to be 50 yards.
Lots of pea to marble size hail accompanied the storm.
